---
title: "Choosing Your Question"
---

When choosing your research question, it’s important to look at all your different
variables and determine what you would like to assess. Pick something that is meaningful to
you, you can connect with, or something that genuinely interests you. When I first started this
project, I scrolled through the dataset and looked at all the different variables and numbers.
There’s many to choose from, so you’ll want to narrow it down significantly. Try not to get
overwhelmed and lost in all the numbers -- take this time to gather ideas. Upon looking through
the dataset, I thought about what I might want to investigate or what story I want to tell. I have
an interest in healthcare deserts and mental health, so it made sense to look at opioid misuse in
rural populations in people with and without mental health disorders. I was able to further narrow
this down to looking at young adults in the south as my sample. This decision allowed for me to
have more connection with this analysis as I could fall into these categories based on my age
and where I live. Overall, the important thing to remember when choosing your question is to
think about the story you want to tell using the data you are given.
